$comment: Authored ledger of Lyra-only public names that change across a major release. Each profile drives lyra-ui-migrate --origin=<origin>, the generated llms/migration.md section and the packaged dist/cli/migration-contract.json. renames and reviews must each match an implemented, deprecated Lyra-only member and its component-metadata.json record (removalNotBefore in aliasRemovalMajor, since no later than toMajor.0.0 or 'unreleased'); defaults, detailChanges and slotContent record changes that have no member deprecation record, and a slotContent entry for a slot whose content carries a slot-content record keeps exactly that record's permittedContent as allow. check-migration-coverage.mjs also requires every Lyra-only deprecation removed in aliasRemovalMajor to have a rename or review entry (a slotContent entry for a slot-content record). Entries stay sorted by tag and name. See docs/rfcs/0003-lyra-v21-migration-profile.md. moduleReviews identify canonical exportDeprecations by kind, module (for named exports/events/attributes) and name, sorted in that order. Replacement guidance and release windows are projected from that metadata, never duplicated here. Module migrations are report-only; check-migration-coverage requires both v21/removal23 and v22/removal24 module cohorts to be complete.

slotContent.summary: Only items, labels and separators belong in the menu list; move other content to slot="header" or slot="footer", which render it outside role="menu".

propertyChanges.summary: Use the string heading levels '1' through '6', or 'none'; numeric JavaScript assignments must be reviewed and converted. HTML heading-level strings remain valid; invalid values now fall back to '3' instead of numeric clamping.
An authored host aria-label now takes precedence over this legacy property, including an explicitly empty host value. Review consumers that set both names.

Size now controls both search chrome and thread rows. Previously size controlled search while compact controlled rows independently; review explicit size and compact combinations, using row styling where independent density must be preserved.
